inputs.sbc_source: TTM to 30-Jun-2026 from SEC XBRL (us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation 236 FY2025 + 123 H1-2026 - 110 H1-2025 = 249) plus cash taxes on net-share settlement (us-gaap:PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation 116 + 126 - 110 = 132). Marriott's adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation adds back share-based compensation only and publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.buyback_note: TTM to 30-Jun-2026: FY2025 3,300 + H1-2026 1,819 - H1-2025 1,500 (kpis.buybacks, financing-activity cash). Marriott is a serial repurchaser: the flat count is funded, not a convention. Dividends ~0.72B/yr on top.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 30-Jun-2026 = 262.2M: cover-page count 260.8M at 2026-07-27 (dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding) rolled back ~0.8M for July repurchases to ~261.6M at 30 June, plus 0.6M dilutive securities (Q2-2026 diluted 264.5M less basic 263.9M). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; the ~$3.6B/yr buyback is the mechanism that keeps it flat and is value-neutral here.
inputs.net_debt_note: Q2-2026 10-Q: long-term debt 16,455 + current portion 460 = 16,915 total debt (incl. ~1,242 commercial paper); cash 462. Operating lease liabilities (~0.96B) are NOT added: lease cost is an operating expense inside the EBITDA margin (treatment A).
inputs.fy0_note: Base revenue is the trailing twelve months to 30-Jun-2026 (FY2025 26,186 + H1-2026 13,725 - H1-2025 13,007 = 26,904) so that the flow base, the balance sheet and the share count all carry the same 30-Jun-2026 vintage; projection year 1 is Jul-2026..Jun-2027. Fiscal year is the calendar year.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rates. Rf 4.1% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.25 (lodging demand beta; revenue halved in 2020) -> cost of equity ~10.3%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.0% (Q1-2026 notes issued at 4.5% and 5.1%), ~3.75% after tax. Market-value weights ~85% equity / 15% debt (equity ~93B, net debt 16.5B) -> WACC ~9.3%; rounded to 9.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is charged once, through the probability weights, not again through per-scenario discount rates.
inputs.lease_treatment: A: operating lease expense stays inside the EBITDA margin; lease liabilities (~0.96B at 31-Dec-2025) are excluded from net debt. Finance leases are immaterial and sit inside the debt line.
inputs.ebitda_basis_note: EBITDA margin paths are PRE-SBC EBITDA on a GAAP basis that INCLUDES the net cost-reimbursement deficit (cost reimbursement revenue less reimbursed expenses), i.e. GAAP operating income + depreciation + amortization + SBC: FY2023 18.6%, FY2024 17.7% (incl. 68 restructuring), FY2025 18.5%, TTM Jun-2026 18.4% (H1-2026 19.4%). Marriott's own adjusted EBITDA (FY2026 guide 5.97-6.03B, ~21.5-22% of revenue) adds the reimbursement deficit back as timing. Cash evidence sits between the two: TTM OCF 3,728 reconciles to adjusted EBITDA less interest and cash taxes with only ~-0.1B of working capital, because the Bonvoy deferred-revenue float funds the GAAP deficit. The base path therefore starts at 19.5% (1pp above the GAAP TTM, giving one-third credit for the deficit reversing) and matures to 20.5%; bull reaches ~22% (adjusted basis fully realised); bear holds ~18.5% (deficit permanent) with a 16.5% trough in the downturn year. Revenue is GROSS revenue including ~18-19B of zero-margin cost reimbursements, which is why the margins look low for a franchisor.
inputs.capex_note: capex_pct_path covers two lines: capital and technology expenditures (TTM 596 = 2.2% of revenue, inflated in 2025-26 by the owner-reimbursed technology transformation) PLUS contract acquisition costs (key money paid to owners to win management/franchise contracts, ~0.3B/yr, ~1.1-1.3%), which Marriott reports in investing activities outside its own FCF definition but which is the growth capex of a franchisor. Base 3.4% tapering to 3.2% as the tech programme rolls off.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route (SKILL.md row 1: operating company, fee-based franchisor/manager). Not BVPS-compounding -- book equity is -4.5B after fifteen years of buybacks and carries no information about value; a book-value anchor would break, so historical equity CAGRs are reported as not meaningful and growth is anchored to revenue/FCF CAGRs and guidance instead. Fresh build, no prior DCF. last_fcf (2,751) is LEVERED owner FCF per the field contract (reported FCF 3,132 - SBC incl. award taxes 381; interest income 42 NOT stripped because the company is deeply net-debt, so it is recorded as 0). The engine builds UNLEVERED owner FCF from components and deducts net debt once; the TTM unlevered equivalent is ~3.39B (2,751 + after-tax interest ~0.64B), or ~3.1B after ~0.3B of key money, i.e. ~11.5% of revenue, against a component year-1 base margin of ~10.6% -- the component build is slightly below cash reality, not above it. Working capital capture 0%: FY2023-FY2025 OCF less (NI + D&A + SBC) was negative in each year (cash taxes above provision through the final TCJA transition-tax instalments) and +0.43B in the TTM; the Bonvoy float is already reflected in the margin basis above, so it is not credited twice. Cash tax 25% on EBIT: GAAP ETR 23.4% FY2025 / 24.6% FY2024; cash taxes ran ~30% of pretax in 2023-25 on transition-tax instalments that ended in 2025 (H1-2026 cash taxes 350 vs 488 provision). Valuation date sits 3 months after the TTM base, so year-1 flows are discounted ~3 months too long -- a small conservative bias.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026 guidance (RevPAR +3.0-3.5%, net rooms growth ~4.5%) applied to gross revenue, cross-checked against H1-2026 revenue +5.5% y/y; equity CAGR unusable
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Shareholders' equity is negative (-4.5B at Q2-2026, negative since FY2011) because cumulative buybacks exceed retained earnings; equity CAGRs are undefined and the equity-anchor rule cannot be applied. 5-year CAGRs start from the FY2020 COVID trough (revenue 10.6B, EPS -0.82) and overstate trend growth: FY2019->FY2025 revenue CAGR is 3.8%. The 3-year CAGRs (FY2022->FY2025: revenue 8.0%, EPS 9.4%, owner FCF 8.8%) still include post-COVID RevPAR recovery and sit above the ~5% run-rate guidance implies.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes): FY2019 697, FY2020 1,200 (COVID year inflated by ~0.9B of prepaid co-brand card cash), FY2021 722, FY2022 1,750, FY2023 2,405, FY2024 1,624 (capex 750 incl. the Sheraton Grand Chicago purchase), FY2025 2,256, TTM Jun-2026 2,751. Owner-FCF 3y CAGR 8.8% vs reported 8.7%: SBC (incl. award taxes) has grown in line with cash flow at ~1.3-1.4% of revenue, so SBC is not eating the growth.

base.narrative: Guidance-anchored: gross revenue +5% in year 1 (RevPAR +3-3.5%, net rooms ~4.5%, reimbursements growing with the system), decelerating to 3% by year 10 as the pipeline matures and US supply growth stays muted. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin 19.5% -> 20.5% on fee mix (franchise and co-brand fees outgrow pass-through reimbursements) and partial reversal of the cost-reimbursement deficit. No recession in the explicit window; cyclicality is carried by the bear weight.

bull.narrative: Net rooms growth sustains 5-6% on the 618k-room pipeline and conversions (citizenM, City Express), RevPAR compounds 3-4% with Middle East drag fading, and the adjusted-EBITDA margin (~22%) is fully realised in cash as the Bonvoy float keeps funding the reimbursement timing. Key money intensity eases as conversions displace new-build.

bear.narrative: A 2001/2009-style lodging downturn in year 2 (RevPAR -9%, gross revenue -5%, incentive fees collapse, reimbursement deficit widens, margin trough 16.5%), a two-year recovery, then slower unit growth (3-4%) as owner financing tightens. Reimbursement deficit treated as a permanent cost (margin caps at 18.5%, the GAAP FY2023-25 level). Not a COVID repeat -- that would put the bear on the terminal floor.

scenario_narratives.base: Marriott compounds as a fee-taker on a growing room base: ~4.5% net unit growth from a record pipeline (over half international), RevPAR +3% a year, and a Bonvoy/co-brand stream that scales with little capital. Gross revenue (which carries ~18-19B of zero-margin reimbursements) grows ~5% fading to 3%; the pre-SBC EBITDA margin on that gross base expands from 19.5% to 20.5% as fee revenue outgrows pass-through. Capex plus key money run ~3.2-3.4% of revenue. No recession is inserted into the explicit ten years; the cycle risk is carried in the bear weight. Gordon value at 9%/3% (17.2x year-10 FCF) sits under the 20x cap, so the cap does not bind.
scenario_narratives.bull: Unit growth holds at 5-6% as conversions and the citizenM/City Express brands widen the funnel, Middle East construction and RevPAR drag fade, and global RevPAR compounds 3-4%. The margin reaches Marriott's own adjusted-EBITDA basis (~22%) because the loyalty float keeps funding the reimbursement timing and incentive fees grow with hotel profitability. Key money intensity eases toward 3% as conversions displace new-builds. Terminal growth 3.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The axes are lodging-demand cyclicality and the GAAP/adjusted margin gap. A demand shock in year 2 (RevPAR -9%, not a COVID-scale collapse) takes gross revenue down 5% and the margin to 16.5% as incentive fees vanish and the reimbursement deficit widens; recovery takes two years and net unit growth slows to 3-4% as owner financing tightens. The reimbursement deficit never reverses, capping the margin at the FY2023-25 GAAP level (~18.5%). Leverage (net debt/EBITDA ~3.4x, negative book equity) means buybacks pause but solvency is not in question; the scenario does not hit the terminal floor.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (house default 15%): lodging has had a demand shock in each of the last three decades (2001, 2009, 2020) so a downturn inside a 10-year window is near base-rate, and the ~3.4x net debt/EBITDA plus negative book equity give the company less room to buy through one than the asset-light label suggests. Bull 25% (default 35%): the bull case needs three independent things -- sustained 5-6% unit growth, 3-4% RevPAR with the Middle East drag gone, and the full adjusted-EBITDA margin showing up in cash -- and Marriott has already guided net rooms growth to the low end of its range on construction delays. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Marriott is valued as what it is -- a stream of management, franchise and co-brand fees on a room base it does not own -- with SBC and net-share-settlement taxes charged as cash, the ~0.3B/yr of key money charged as growth capex, and the EBITDA basis held between GAAP (reimbursement deficit as a cost) and Marriott's adjusted definition (deficit as timing). The flows are unlevered and the 16.5B of net debt is deducted once at 9% WACC. Book equity is negative and ignored. The headline finding is a discount-rate gap: the owner-FCF value at 9%/3% is well below the market price, which capitalises ~3.3B of company-defined FCF at ~30x and relies on debt-assisted buybacks for mid-teens EPS growth. Street basis (SBC as non-cash) adds the PV of ~0.4B/yr of SBC and does not close the gap; the required-return table shows the rate the current price implies.
key_risks_to_valuation: Discount-rate sensitivity: ~60% of EV is terminal value; each 1pp of WACC moves the base value materially (see sensitivity grid)
Margin basis: if the cost-reimbursement deficit is genuinely permanent, the base margin path (19.5->20.5%) is ~1-2pp too generous; if it is pure timing, the bull (22%) is the right anchor
Key money: contract acquisition costs are modelled inside capex at ~1.1-1.3% of revenue from memory of the FY2025 10-K investing section rather than a parsed line; +/-0.1B/yr is ~+/-$4/share
Lodging demand cyclicality: a COVID-scale shock (revenue -50%) is outside the bear case; the bear models a 2001/2009-style RevPAR -9% year

Leverage: 16.9B debt against 0.5B cash and negative book equity; buybacks are partly debt-funded (FY2025 net debt +1.8B against 3.3B repurchased), so a credit-market closure stops the flat-share-count mechanism

Valuation vintage: flows are TTM to 30-Jun-2026 and the balance sheet is 30-Jun-2026; the Q3-2026 10-Q (late Oct/early Nov 2026) will move net debt up ~0.5-1.0B on continued buybacks and the diluted count down ~2-3M
